story.title: Ferry Fire in the Philippines Leaves Five Dead and Dozens Missing
story.summary: A fire on a passenger ferry near Coron in the Philippines has resulted in at least five fatalities and left 87 individuals missing. Coast guard crews are conducting searches in challenging sea conditions, with reports indicating that over 40 people have been rescued. The incident occurred near a popular tourist destination in the province of Palawan.

explore_lenses.label: Why did the death toll rise so quickly?
explore_lenses.title: Access to the vessel changed the count
explore_lenses.summary: The initial missing-person total was based on the ferry manifest while responders could not safely enter the smoke-filled vessel; once they gained access, they recovered additional remains.

claims.text: By September 11, the confirmed death toll had risen to at least 35, with 54 people still missing and 43 survivors reported.
Rescuers initially struggled to board because of heat and thick smoke, which delayed searches of areas where passengers may have been trapped.
The earlier figures were explicitly provisional: the coast guard said its count was based on the 134-person manifest and could change during search-and-rescue operations.

explore_lenses.label: What may have caused the fire?
explore_lenses.title: Cargo hold is a lead, not a conclusion
explore_lenses.summary: Investigators have not established a cause. Survivor accounts point to an apparent explosion in or near the cargo area, while authorities are also examining compliance questions.

claims.text: The Philippine Coast Guard had not determined the fire’s cause as of September 11.
A survivor told officials there was a loud explosion followed by smoke and fire; local reporting said the account placed the explosion in the cargo hold, where vehicles and goods were being carried.

The coast guard is examining possible violations, including whether the vessel was overloaded and whether passengers had life jackets; some survivors were found without life jackets, according to its spokesperson.
The vessel had passed a pre-departure inspection, according to the coast guard, and was carrying 134 people—well below its reported certified capacity of 333.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next for families and rescuers?
explore_lenses.title: Search, identification and investigation continue
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate priorities are locating people who may have drifted away or remained aboard, identifying victims, and preserving evidence from the damaged ferry once conditions permit.

claims.text: The coast guard deployed its vessels and response boats alongside military, government, volunteer and fishing boats; it also alerted nearby ships and coastal villages to watch for people who may have drifted ashore.
Bad weather, large waves and strong currents complicated the response and moved the distressed vessel farther from Turda, affecting both the search area and access to the ship.

Forecast: The casualty and missing totals may continue to change as responders complete vessel searches and authorities verify the manifest against survivors and recovered victims, according to coast guard spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab.
Atienza Interisland Ferries Inc. said its stated priority was the safety and well-being of those aboard and that it had mobilized resources to manage the crisis.

story_report.summary: At least 35 people were confirmed dead after a passenger ferry caught fire near Coron in Palawan, Philippines, and 54 others remained missing as of September 11. Authorities reported 43 survivors, but said the toll could still change while crews search the vessel and reconcile the passenger list with survivors and recovered victims. The earlier count of five dead and 87 missing was provisional and based on a 134-person manifest.

sections.heading: Rescue Operations Face Rough Seas
sections.body: Coast guard vessels and response boats were joined by military, government, volunteer and fishing boats in the search. Nearby ships and coastal villages were alerted to watch for people who may have drifted ashore. Bad weather, high waves and strong currents complicated access to the ferry and shifted it farther from Turda, expanding the area responders needed to cover.

sections.heading: Fire Cause and Safety Under Review
sections.body: The Philippine Coast Guard had not determined what caused the fire as of September 11. One survivor told officials a loud explosion was followed by smoke and flames; local reporting placed the reported explosion in the cargo hold, where vehicles and goods were carried. The coast guard is also examining possible safety violations, including life-jacket use, although it said the vessel had passed a pre-departure inspection and carried 134 people, below its reported 333-person certified capacity.

unresolved.text: Authorities still need to identify recovered remains and establish a final passenger-and-crew count; two people listed on the manifest reportedly did not board.
The ignition source, any safety violations and potential legal responsibility remain undetermined, and no public timetable has been reported for the investigation, recovery or enforcement action.

related_stories.title: Commemorating the 25th Anniversary of the September 11 Attacks
related_stories.summary: On the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, ceremonies were held across the United States to honor the nearly 3,000 victims. President Donald Trump attended a ceremony at the Pentagon, while Vice President JD Vance and four former presidents participated in commemorations at Ground Zero in New York. The day was marked by a somber mood as families of victims read the names of those lost in the attacks.

related_stories.title: Fire in Bukavu Claims Lives of Schoolchildren and Destroys Neighborhood
related_stories.summary: A devastating fire in the Kadutu district of Bukavu, Democratic Republic of Congo, has resulted in the deaths of at least 24 schoolchildren. The blaze engulfed two schools and destroyed over 300 homes, leading to a chaotic stampede as people attempted to escape the flames.

related_stories.title: Brother of NYPD Officer Who Died from 9/11-Related Cancer Advocates for Victims
related_stories.summary: As the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks approaches, Phil Alvarez, a retired NYPD detective, reflects on his brother Luis's death from cancer linked to toxins at Ground Zero. Alvarez is working to extend the September 11th Victim Compensation Fund to assist others affected by similar health issues. This year, a seventh moment of silence will be observed to honor those who have died from illnesses related to the toxic dust from the attacks.

related_stories.title: Fatal Tour Bus Crash in Swiss Alps Claims Five Lives
related_stories.summary: A tour bus carrying 45 Dutch tourists overturned in a construction zone in the Swiss Alps, resulting in five fatalities and numerous injuries. The incident occurred in a south-eastern region of Switzerland, highlighting the dangers associated with mountainous travel.
